instructions:
1. Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Keep your back flat and core braced.
3. Keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, lift one leg out to the side until the thigh is near parallel to the floor.
4. Keep hips level and do not rotate the torso.
5. Lower the leg back down with control, then switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move only at the hip; keep the spine and torso still.
2. Squeeze the outer glute at the top of each lift.
3. Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
4. Work on a non-slip surface for stable hand and knee contact.

instructions:
1. Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Keep your back flat and core braced.
3. Keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, lift one leg out to the side until the thigh is near parallel to the floor.
4. Draw small controlled circles with the knee while keeping hips level.
5. Reverse the circle direction, then lower the leg and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the circles small and controlled to stay in the hip.
2. Do not let the hips tilt or the torso rotate.
3. Squeeze the outer glute throughout the circles.
4. Breathe steadily and avoid holding your breath.

instructions:
1. Stand facing a fixed bar and grip it with both hands at about chest height.
2. Step back and bend your knees, keeping your arms straight.
3. Push your hips backward and let your upper body lean away from the bar.
4. Drop your chest down to deepen the stretch through the lats and shoulders.
5. Hold briefly, breathing slowly.
6. Step forward to release. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move into the stretch slowly and avoid bouncing.
2. Only go as far as a comfortable stretch, never into pain.
3. Make sure the bar is secure and can hold your weight.
4. Keep the spine long rather than rounding the lower back.

instructions:
1. Set a flat bench between two low cable pulleys and attach a handle to each.
2. Lie back on the bench with feet flat on the floor.
3. Hold a handle in each hand with arms out to the sides and a slight bend in the elbows.
4. Sweep the handles up over your chest in a wide arc until they meet.
5. Squeeze the chest, then lower the handles back out with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a fixed slight bend in the elbows the whole time.
2. Drive the movement with the chest, not the arms.
3. Inhale as you lower, exhale as you bring the handles together.
4. Keep shoulder blades pulled back and down on the bench.

instructions:
1. Lie on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
2. Run a resistance band under your upper back and hold a handle in each hand.
3. Bend your elbows so your upper arms rest on the floor at about 90 degrees.
4. Press the handles straight up until the arms are extended.
5. Lower the handles back until the upper arms touch the floor.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
2. Pause briefly when the elbows touch the floor for control.
3. Choose a band tension that lets you keep clean form.
4. Drive through the chest while keeping the wrists stacked over the elbows.
